One-on-One AI Trainers Imagine having a personal conversational AI trainer with you anytime you need it on any topic. It is a subject matter expert on anything you need or want to learn and understand, but it is also trained to behave as an expert Socratic teacher rather than just a lecturer. It asks you questions and explores topics with you until the learning-required epiphanies occur. This idea is not theoretical for me. As we talked about early in the book, since 2010, I’ve had the privilege of leading a team at the forefront of advanced brain science–based learning systems, and we now hold three patents around scalable conversational AI instructors/ trainers integrated with deep principles of brain science of human learning and brought a new kind of AI trainer to market as of late 2025. And as you will not be surprised at this point, our AI is also trained to handle the interaction with the learner in a nuanced way that is designed to optimize the engagement of the hippocampus to support enduring long-term memory, not just short-term understanding. Ambient AI in Healthcare In one of my largest areas of focus, healthcare training, there is a great deal of promising work happening right now around ambient AI—particularly as it relates to the physician–patient interaction. Ambient AI refers to AI that is on and listening and able to respond to requests with the full context of the discussion already underway. As a backstory, a few years ago, I was in a medical office visit with a close friend for a minor issue that turned out fine. As I listened to her very good internal medicine doctor talking about the next steps in her care, I texted with my AI on my phone and told it what the next steps were. With her permission, I had loaded her medical history into the AI, and it suggested that, because of an item five years back in her medical history, it was important to run a specific test before moving forward with the plan. I gently asked a question of the doctor: “Would it be important to know that she had this thing five years earlier?” The doctor paused and then said, “Yes. That is very important. We will need to run this certain test before proceeding.” The problem was that a doctor simply does not have the time to go that far back into a chart. But that is changing with ambient AI. I believe we are rapidly approaching a time when AI will be present in nearly every doctor’s visit—not as a cold interface, but as an intelligent presence that reads your entire chart before the visit, highlights relevant information for the physician, observes the visit in real time, maps any new insights to the existing record, orders labs or tests the doctor asks for, and then generates clinical notes and prescriptions automatically. The result: more informed doctors who have more time to focus on the patient and spend less time typing in the medical record during the appointment. Simple, but high impact. That technology exists today. It would not surprise me if almost everyone who reads this book in 2026 has already had the experience of their doctor bringing ambient AI into the room. And at our many large health system clients, this technology is rapidly being deployed at an institutional scale in their hospitals. Importantly, it is helping solve the very real problem of physician burnout resulting from too much time in medical records and too little time with patients. When physicians have to write up their medical record notes at home after the kids have gone to bed, they call it “pajama time documentation.” This will rapidly become a thing of the past. In short, the AI becomes a silent partner—unseen, but profoundly impactful. The days of doctors spending large portions of their visit interacting with rigid, structured databases of electronic health records are coming to an end. Soon, their focus will return to where it belongs: the patient. An Incredible External Brain In the spring of 2025, two people sat down to discuss the next generation of human-to-computer interfaces. 84 One was Sam Altman, the CEO at OpenAI, which developed ChatGPT. The other was Jony Ive, who famously designed the iPhone and iPad as the lead designer at Apple. Sam said: 85 When you talk to people who use our latest model and say that this is, like, genius level in every field and you just have to put in the work to like pull it all together, but if you have a hard problem you can have these like geniuses in all of the different disciplines and they report: “I’m two or three times more productive as a scientist than I was before.” “I’m two or three times faster to find a cure for cancer than I was before, because I have this incredible external brain.” That just didn’t exist six months ago. I think this will be one of these moments of just an absolute embarrassment of riches of what people go and create for collective society. Jony Ive, perhaps the greatest product designer of our time, added, “I am absolutely certain that we are literally on the brink of a new generation of technology that can make us our better selves.” 86 AI Agents with Agency We’re also entering an era where AI will not only observe and advise—it will also act. The next frontier isn’t just conversational AI or passive reflection. It’s a new class of intelligent agents: systems that don’t just understand what you want but go out and get it done.
